title: Los Angeles Rams trade for Trent McDuffie - NewsBreak
text:
By Jack Sabin ,
9 hours ago The Los Angeles Rams have made a big trade in trading for All-Pro CB Trent McDuffie. Does this actually make sense? Let’s find out (Gif via Giphy) Los Angeles Rams trade for Trent McDuffie The Los Angeles Rams make their blockbuster move of the offseason by trading for All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie. Adam Schefter was the first to break the news and reveal the full package.
Right away, you may think this is a slam-dunk trade for the Rams. Their secondary was a weakness for them at times due mainly to how young they are at the position. So bringing in a guy like McDuffie seems like the perfect solution to that right?
From a pure talent preseptive you could make that argument. Nobody is doubting the ability of McDuffie. He is a proven All-Pro talent who has played a part in the Chiefs being Super Bowl contenders year in and year out.
My only issue is the price the Rams are paying and I don’t just mean in this trade. I could tell you, however Trey already made a video explaining why this trade doesn’t make a lot of sense for the Rams.
@treydaubert My thoughts to the Rams trading for Trent McDuffie #trentmcduffie #rams #chiefs #2026nfldraft #nfl
♬ original sound – Trey Daubert Trey does a great job of summarizing this trade. The biggest thing to me is the lack of leverage the Rams now have when negotiating.
Trent McDuffie now knows you just gave up all that draft capital to get him, so he knows he can bleed them out of as much money as he wants, so this doesn’t end up looking like a massive overpay for a short-term rental.
I wouldn’t quite say this trade is an F for the Rams though. McDuffie is a great olayer and will certainly address a weakness this Rams team has. As he mentioned, they do have that extra first this year courtesy of the Falcons.
But even with all that in mind, this seems like a bit of an overpay, especially when you look at the talent coming out of the Draft this year. The safeties this year look like freaks of nature with a lot of corners seeing their stock rise as well .
Meaning the Rams could have very easily addressed this weakness in their secondary with the two first they would have had. Heck, they could have even gone with a cheaper option in free agency or via trade.
Instead, they wanted the big shiny object and if they don’t win the big game here in the next couple of years, this trade will only look worse. The Rams do have a fair amount of cap space. But that will quickly dry up after they extend guys like Puka Nacua or the entirety of their defensive line that will be up for contract soon.
Breece Hall Has Been Tagged That cap space is going to dry up very quickly. Now with the addition of McDuffie, they will see it disappear even more quickly. Meaning they will likely have to make compromises at other positions.
None of this is meant to be a diss against Trent McDuffie. I think he is a great player. Trey and I feel like the Rams gave up way too much for a guy they now have to extend while having no leverage.
I guess if the Rams can win the Super Bowl in the next year or two, they can say it’s worth it. They were sooo close. So maybe this move is what gets them over the hump. If not? The Rams will have some difficult decisions to make in the coming years.
